# Xpenses — Architecture Reference

> Full context document for AI agents. Keep this file up to date when making structural changes.

## Continuity: Savings Goals MVP (2026-10-01)

This section describes the new implementation and supersedes historical savings and permissions references below. Earlier sections describe previous project states; always compare them with current code and rules. [Project guidelines](../docs/project-guidelines.md) are canonical for current conventions and contracts; [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) defines operational rules.

- Lazy route `/metas` → `SavingsGoalsModule`, accessible through the menu and Dashboard summary. Reactive forms and ng-bootstrap modals use a mobile-first design with Lato and existing brown tokens.
- `SavingsGoal` / `SavingsTransaction` contracts in `core/models/savings-goal.ts` use numeric integer CLP amounts only for these new collections. Historical models retain their types.
- `SavingsGoalsService`: reactive reads tied to Firebase Auth; data under `users/{uid}/savings-goals`, `savings-transactions`, and `savings-planning/state`. Contributions and withdrawals are manual; balance and history commit in an atomic transaction. Stable submission IDs support retries. Withdrawals cannot exceed the balance; contributions require active goals.
- Planning uses percentages or fixed amounts. The aggregate percentage of active goals is serialized in the `state` document to prevent concurrent saves from exceeding 100%. Pausing, completing, or archiving releases the percentage while preserving balance and history.
- Pure functions in `core/utils/savings-goals.utils.ts` handle suggestions, summaries, dates, and projections. Plans differ from recorded savings. Estimated dates exclude interest and returns.
- Income remains global and independent of payment methods. `IncomesService.getAll()` now cancels and switches reads with Firebase Auth, avoiding cached-user dependencies when sessions change.
- `SavingsSummaryModule` contains the global Dashboard summary: current balance across all goals, contributions minus withdrawals in the selected calendar month, and the current plan applied to that month's income. Switching cards leaves these values unchanged; changing months changes the transactions. Historical plan snapshots are unavailable.
- The Dashboard distinguishes income margin and suggested reserves from recorded contributions. Savings are neither added to expenses nor deducted from the budget again.
- Current Firestore rules recursively authorize owners under `users/{userId}` and already cover the new collections. Business restrictions and transaction immutability are enforced by the client service, not server antifraud rules. The previous schema is preserved; remote data is not migrated.
- Transactions require a connection; errors preserve forms for retry. Existing local persistence does not make transactions available offline.
- New tests use synthetic data without real Firebase access; run `npm run build` and `npm test -- --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`. An unavailable Angular Material theme reference was removed from the test target; actual application styles were retained.
- Hosting was published on 2026-10-01 to `xpenses-93552` with owner authorization, a successful build, and 29 passing tests. Published rules were checked against local rules and were not redeployed. Evidence and pending work: [Savings MVP validation](../docs/savings-mvp-validation.md).

## Project Overview

**Xpenses** is a personal finance PWA built with Angular 16 + Firebase. It tracks variable expenses, fixed expenses, income, and subscriptions within a **19th-to-18th billing cycle**. Deployed to Firebase Hosting at `https://xpenses-93552.web.app/`.

| Layer         | Technology                                      |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Framework     | Angular 16.0.4 (NgModule-based, no standalone)  |
| UI            | Bootstrap 4 + ng-bootstrap 15                   |
| Icons         | Font Awesome 6 (`fas`, `fa-solid`, `fa-regular`)|
| Database      | Firebase Firestore (AngularFire 7.6.1)          |
| Auth          | Firebase Authentication (email/password)        |
| Hosting       | Firebase Hosting                                |
| PWA           | @angular/service-worker 16.0.4                  |
| Offline       | IndexedDB persistence via `enableIndexedDbPersistence()` |
| SCSS          | Bootstrap 4 + custom design tokens              |
| State         | No NgRx — raw Observables + RxJS                |

## Repository Structure

```
src/
  app/
    app.module.ts           # Root module; wires ServiceWorker + Firestore persistence
    app-routing.module.ts   # Two top-level lazy routes: /auth, /
    auth/                   # Login, Register, Reset — no guard
    core/                   # Guards, models, services, validators
    main/                   # Shell layout + sidebar; lazy-loads feature modules
    dashboard/
    expenses/
    fixed-expenses/
    incomes/
    subscriptions/
    shared/                 # SharedModule — re-exported to all feature modules
  assets/sass/              # Global SCSS design tokens
  environments/             # environment.ts (prod) + environment.development.ts
firestore.rules             # Firestore security rules
ngsw-config.json            # Service worker caching strategy
firebase.json               # Firebase Hosting config + cache headers
```

---

## Routing

```
/auth/login        → LoginComponent      (no guard)
/auth/register     → RegisterComponent   (no guard)
/auth/reset        → ResetComponent      (no guard)

/                  → MainComponent       (inline CanMatch — redirects to /auth/login if not authenticated)
/dashboard         → DashboardModule
/ingresos          → IncomesModule
/gastos            → ExpensesModule
/gastos-fijos      → FixedExpensesModule
/subscripciones    → SubscriptionsModule
```

**Auth guard implementation:** inline function in `main-routing.module.ts` using `inject(AuthService).isAuthenticated()`. The class-based `AuthGuard` in `core/guards/auth.guard.ts` has a capitalisation bug (`CanMatch` vs `canMatch`) — it is **not used**.

**Dead guards:**
- `NoAuthGuard` — references `/empresas` (non-existent). Do not use.
- `IsActiveGuard` — email verification guard, imported but not wired to any route.

## Domain Models

All models extend `Base`:

```typescript
interface Base {
  createdAt: Timestamp;  // Firestore Timestamp
  updatedAt: Timestamp;
  uid?: string;          // Firestore document ID (injected via idField)
}
```

| Model           | Extra fields                                              |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `Expense`       | `title: string`, `amount: string`, `category: ExpenseCategory`, `comment: string` |
| `FixedExpense`  | `title: string`, `amount: string`                         |
| `Income`        | `title: string`, `amount: string`                         |
| `Subscription`  | `title: string`, `amount: string`                         |
| `IUser`         | `name`, `email`, `username`, `image`, `uid?`, `createdAt?` |
| `UserPreferences` | `billingCycleDay: number`, `savingsRate: number`, `variableRate: number` |

> **Critical:** `amount` is always `string`, not `number`, on every model. Never store it as a number.

### ExpenseCategory enum

```
Supermercado | Subscripciones | Transporte | Casa | Cuentas |
Entretenimiento | Otros | Ropa | Auto cuidado | Gasto Fijo
```

### UserPreferences defaults

```typescript
{ billingCycleDay: 19, savingsRate: 20, variableRate: 50 }
```

Stored at `users/{uid}/settings/preferences`. Read via `UserPreferencesService.getPreferences()` (returns `Observable<UserPreferences>` merged with defaults).

## Firestore Collections

### Schema

```
users/{uid}                          ← user document
users/{uid}/expenses/{id}            ← Expense
users/{uid}/fixed-expenses/{id}      ← FixedExpense
users/{uid}/incomes/{id}             ← Income
users/{uid}/subscriptions/{id}       ← Subscription
users/{uid}/settings/preferences     ← UserPreferences (single doc)
```

There is also a top-level `expenses/{expenseId}` collection allowed in the rules — this is **legacy and not used** by the app.

### Querying pattern (all services)

```typescript
// Build path synchronously — never subscribe for the uid
const userId = this.userService.currentUserValue.uid;
const colRef = collection(this.firestore, `users/${userId}/expenses`) as CollectionReference<Expense>;
const q = query(colRef, orderBy('createdAt', 'desc'), where('createdAt', '>=', start), where('createdAt', '<=', end));
return collectionData(q, { idField: 'uid' }) as Observable<Expense[]>;
```

### Write pattern

```typescript
save(item: T) {
  item.createdAt = Timestamp.now();
  item.updatedAt = Timestamp.now();
  return addDoc(colRef, item);
}
update(item: T) {
  item.updatedAt = Timestamp.now();
  return updateDoc(docRef, { ...item });
}
delete(id: string) { return deleteDoc(docRef); }
```

## Firestore Security Rules

File: `firestore.rules`

**Current state:** All authenticated users can read/write any path. Rules check `isAuthenticated()` but do **not** scope to `request.auth.uid == userId`.

```
⚠️ SECURITY GAP: Any logged-in user can read/write another user's data.
   Rules should be tightened to: allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userId;
   before the app is exposed to untrusted users.
```

Protected paths:
- `users/{userId}` — read + write
- `users/{userId}/expenses/{expenseId}` — read + write
- `users/{userId}/fixed-expenses/{fixedExpenseId}` — read + write
- `users/{userId}/incomes/{incomeId}` — read + write (also has a bare `users/{userId}/incomes` rule)
- `users/{userId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` — read + write
- `users/{userId}/settings/preferences` — read + write
- `expenses/{expenseId}` — read + write (legacy, top-level collection)

## Services

| Service                    | Responsibility                                      |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `AuthService`              | `login()`, `register()`, `logout()`, `resetPassword()`, `isAuthenticated(): Observable<User\|null>` |
| `UserService`              | Holds current user; exposes `currentUser` (Observable) and `currentUserValue` (sync) |
| `ExpensesService`          | CRUD for `expenses`; `getAll(start?, end?)` defaults to current billing cycle |
| `FixedExpensesService`     | CRUD for `fixed-expenses`                           |
| `IncomesService`           | CRUD for `incomes`                                  |
| `SubscriptionsService`     | CRUD for `subscriptions`                            |
| `UserPreferencesService`   | `getPreferences()` / `savePreferences()`            |

All services are `providedIn: 'root'` and use `inject()` for DI.

## Billing Cycle Logic

> Historical description: the current Dashboard uses the selected card's configured cycle day, while the default expense-service fallback still uses day 19. Current cycle boundaries and installment attribution are defined in [Project guidelines](../docs/project-guidelines.md#dashboard--billing-periods).

The default billing window is **day 19 of current month → day 18 of next month**.

```typescript
if (currentDay >= 19) {
  start = new Date(year, month, 19, 0,0,0,0);
  end   = new Date(year, month + 1, 18, 23,59,59,999);
} else {
  start = new Date(year, month - 1, 19, 0,0,0,0);
  end   = new Date(year, month, 18, 23,59,59,999);
}
```

This logic is hardcoded in `ExpensesService.getAll()` and **duplicated** in `DashboardComponent`. `UserPreferences.billingCycleDay` exists but services don't consume it yet.

## Authentication Flow

1. `Firebase Auth` (email + password only)
2. On register: `sendEmailVerification()` is called but **not enforced** (no guard checks it)
3. Password reset: `sendPasswordResetEmail()` with redirect to `{appUrl}/login`
4. On logout: `localStorage.clear()` + `afAuth.signOut()`
5. `UserService` listens to `authState` and keeps a `BehaviorSubject<IUser>` — always use `.currentUserValue` synchronously when building Firestore paths

## Feature Module Pattern

Each feature follows this structure:

```
feature/
  feature.module.ts           # declares XComponent, AddXComponent, EditXComponent; imports SharedModule
  feature-routing.module.ts
  feature.component.ts/html/scss   # list + pagination + open modal
  add-feature/
    add-feature.component.ts       # FormGroup + EventEmitter<T> newItem$; closes modal on submit
  edit-feature/
    edit-feature.component.ts      # @Input() item; FormGroup; EventEmitter<T> editItem$; EventEmitter<string> deleteItem$
```

**Modal pattern:**
- Parent opens modal via `NgbModal.open(AddXComponent)`
- Gets `EventEmitter` from `componentInstance`
- Subscribes with `.pipe(take(1))` and calls service on emit
- Add component: `ViewEncapsulation.None`, host class `.add-x-modal`
- Edit component: `ViewEncapsulation.None`, host class `.edit-x-modal`
- Auto-focus first field with `ngbAutofocus` directive (not `autofocus` attribute)
- Two-step delete confirmation: first click sets `confirmingDelete = true`, second click emits

### Design Conventions
- Font: `Lato`
- Import tokens: `@import "src/assets/sass/variables"` at top of component SCSS
- Modal max-width: `32rem`
- Border-radius standard: `8px` (inputs, buttons, cards) / `14px` (modal)
- Focus ring: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(189,153,136, 0.2)` (brand-secondary)
- Valid state: `border-color: rgba(46,125,50,0.5)` + green glow
- Error color: `#c62828`
- Animations: `fadeSlideUp`, `skeletonPulse`, `rowSlideIn`, `modalFadeUp` — all have `prefers-reduced-motion` overrides

## PWA / Service Worker

- Config: `ngsw-config.json` — `updateMode: "prefetch"` on app shell; Google Fonts dataGroups (stylesheets 1d, font files 14d)
- Enabled: `!isDevMode()` (disabled in `ng serve`)
- Offline persistence: `enableIndexedDbPersistence()` in `app.module.ts`
- Firebase Hosting no-cache headers on `ngsw-worker.js`, `ngsw.json`, `safety-worker.js`
- `manifest.webmanifest`: `start_url: "/dashboard"`, `theme_color: "#876656"`, `background_color: "#f5f1ee"`
